implementation.name: original-v1-grad-accumulation
implementation.scope: Same three micro-batches as the original. Equal-size micro-batches; each gradient is from a sum-reduced loss, so their sum gives the full-batch sum gradient. No parameter update between micro-batches. Saved-activation labels indicate schematic storage, not a complete memory budget.
implementation.question: What survives between micro-batches?

storyboard.label: Empty accumulator
storyboard.description: Weights start at θ₀. No micro-batch activations or gradient contributions are retained.

storyboard.label: Forward micro-batch 1
storyboard.description: Only batch 1 activations are allocated for its backward consumers.

storyboard.label: Backward micro-batch 1
storyboard.description: Backward adds g₁ to the persistent accumulator. Batch 1 activations can be released after their last consumers.

storyboard.label: Forward micro-batch 2
storyboard.description: Batch 2 creates new activations while g₁ remains in the same accumulator.

storyboard.label: Backward micro-batch 2
storyboard.description: Add g₂ without changing the weights. Batch 2 activations are released.

storyboard.label: Forward micro-batch 3
storyboard.description: Batch 3 uses the same θ₀; accumulated earlier contributions remain live.

storyboard.label: Backward micro-batch 3
storyboard.description: Add g₃ and release batch 3 activations. All examples now contribute to one gradient.

storyboard.label: Update parameters once
storyboard.description: The optimizer consumes the accumulated gradient to produce θ₁. Clearing gradients is a separate action.

storyboard.label: Clear for next logical batch
storyboard.description: The optimizer step is complete; the accumulator is reset before another logical batch.

guard: Sum-reduced equal micro-batches; no claim that batch-dependent layers, dropout, or arithmetic order are identical to a large batch.
